claims.text: Surface compositional segregation governs the initiation of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Surface compositional segregation governs the progression of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Surface compositional segregation enables a liquid-like surface layer to form at premelting temperatures.
An ultrathin inert surface coating can suppress or reduce compositional surface segregation.
Suppressing surface segregation will delay the onset of premelting.
Suppressing surface segregation will alter melting kinetics.
In untreated FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles, surface segregation locally increases atomic mobility.
The increased local atomic mobility causes early nucleation of a liquid-like surface layer.
Segregation-suppressing passivation allows nanoparticles to remain uniformly solid to higher temperatures.
Delayed formation of the liquid-like surface layer subsequently delays full melting.
Untreated nanoparticles will form an observable liquid-like surface layer at lower temperatures than passivated nanoparticles.
Untreated nanoparticles will display faster melting kinetics than passivated nanoparticles.
Passivated nanoparticles will exhibit a higher premelting onset temperature than untreated nanoparticles.
Passivated nanoparticles will show slower and more gradual melting progression.
The proposed comparison is limited to nanoparticles of approximately 12 nm under an inert atmosphere and an identical heating rate.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in premelting onset temperature or altered melting kinetics after passivation would falsify the proposed governing role of surface segregation.
